# Badge

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

media and display · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a short status beside the thing it describes: Paid, Pending, Draft, a count. It is a
label, not a control; for something the user can remove or press, use a Tag or a Button.

```tsx
<Badge tone="success"><Svg icon={checkCircle} />Paid</Badge>
<Badge tone="warning">Pending</Badge>
<Badge tone="danger" variant="solid">Overdue</Badge>
```

Badge has no ARIA role, so the text must carry the meaning; colour alone never does. A long
label truncates to its container instead of wrapping, and `BadgeSkeleton` holds its place
at the same height while data loads.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Badge } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | no | `ReactNode` | - | The label, and any icon beside it. The text carries the meaning; colour never does alone. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The shared size scale; custom emits no size classes. |
| `tone` | no | `primary` \| `neutral` \| `success` \| `warning` \| `danger` \| `info` | `"primary"` | The meaning it signals, which picks its colour ramp. |
| `variant` | no | `solid` \| `soft` \| `outline` | `"soft"` | How loudly the badge stands out: a fill, a tint or an outline. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
